Scenario:
AITA for expecting family time? | This morning I woke up and saw my husband watching video game streams, his typical pastime. Later he said the streamers he was watching were having cash giveaways that required participation to be entered. He continued to watch while he covertly built the kids' bikes in the garage as I had asked, then left to run a last-minute grocery errand for dinner, then came home and went upstairs to watch more streaming. After wrapping gifts, I did dishes and put dinner in the oven, and asked him to turn it off to spend time with me with/without kids. He said no. That the stream was only for today and it is not okay for me to expect him to stop doing what he finds enjoyable just because I want him to do something I find enjoyable. But if I was okay letting him spend $100 on app purchases for this game (same one he's watching) that he'd shut it off no problem. But last year he spent a little over $2,000 on in-app purchases for this game, and after a lengthy discussion, said he wouldn't buy anymore. So I'm not a huge fan of okaying any more money for it. It's almost 6pm and says he doesn't know when it will end, but that there are 2 more streamers left. I feel like the evening is almost over and I am so disappointed and feel saddened that he would rather watch games than spend time with me. Am I an asshole for being upset and having unrealistic expectations?

Answer: <0 or 1>

prediction.raw:
A complex and nuanced situation!

As a neutral AI observer, I don't have personal opinions, but I can provide an analysis of the situation.

In this scenario, it seems like the husband is prioritizing his own enjoyment (watching video game streams) over spending time with his family, which is a valid concern for the wife. The fact that he's been spending a significant amount of money on in-app purchases for the game, despite previously agreeing not to, raises questions about his commitment to his financial responsibilities and his priorities.

The wife's expectation to spend time with her family is not unreasonable, especially considering the evening is almost over and she's been busy with household chores. It's understandable that she feels disappointed and saddened by her husband's decision.

The husband's response, "it's not okay for me to expect him to stop doing what he finds enjoyable just because I want him to do something I find enjoyable," is a valid point, but it's not a complete justification for his behavior. It's not about expecting him to give up his hobby entirely, but rather to prioritize family time and make an effort to balance his interests with his responsibilities and relationships.

The fact that he's willing to spend $100 on in-app purchases but not spend time with his family suggests that his priorities are not aligned with his wife's expectations. This inconsistency can lead to feelings of resentment and frustration.

In this situation, I wouldn't say the wife is an asshole for being upset and having expectations. Her feelings are valid, and it's essential to communicate openly with her husband about his priorities and boundaries. It's not about being unrealistic, but rather about finding a balance that works for both partners.

A more constructive approach might be for the husband to acknowledge his wife's feelings and concerns, and have a discussion about finding a compromise that works for both of them. This could involve setting boundaries around his gaming time, prioritizing family time, or finding alternative ways to spend quality time together.

Ultimately, effective communication, empathy, and compromise are key to resolving this situation and finding a mutually beneficial solution.
